cells.remarks: States that Mutta'yyā, son of Aṇṇu Ayyan of Vaikuṇṭammāḷ-puram, made a gift of the village of Acholampāḍu to Mutta-iyyan, son of Kārttigai Muttayyan of Muccukkuṭṭi, for conducting the worship of the deity called Uṭaiyamārttaṇḍa-kaḷḷiñjūṭu in the temple of Subrahmaṇya. The donee was required to meet the expenses of the worship and also to feed four Brāhmaṇas. One of the clauses of the gift deed states that the right of cultivating the village of Acholampāḍu of Aṭṭaṅgai rested solely in Tiruveṅkaṭam Piḷḷai, son of Subrahmanya Piḷḷai of Āḷvār Tirunagari, who had formerly exercised that right.

There is a later endorsement added to the document proper which registers another land-grant to the same donee by the mother of a king whose name is doubtful. The characters belong to the 6th or 7th century A.C., and the above endorse-ment is engraved in the 8th century A.C. Published. Published in the Journal of the Kalinga Historical Research Society, Vol. II, Nos. 2-3.

cells.remarks: States that the image was made by Śiṅgaṭi Mīhuka, a devotee of Viṣṇu. The sculptor was Jāśōdhara, son of Subhaṅkara. In characters of about the 10th century.
